args.note:
ARGR_ECOLI N-terminal winged-helix DBD, 69 aa (= full-length ArgR residues 7-75; candidate numbering is 1-based on the supplied 69-mer, verified: every candidate's stated WT matches the query at that index).

CHANNELS RUN
- ESM-2 650M masked-marginal: all 100 candidates (uniform coverage; used as the `ranking` score).
- PSSM + Shannon conservation from a 22-row query-anchored MSA (blast_msa call_id:2a71831dfb3a4c00a448c1931ddf1d56); homologs are distant (~29-34% id), so MSA evidence is weaker than usual.
- ESM-IF1 on the supplied AF2 backbone, 18 finalists. Tool returns whole-sequence mean log-likelihood, so I report delta vs WT (WT mean LL -1.4952999612559443, call_id:d2de9cb87ee34326935f5a70d925aa76) x 69 residues as an approximate substitution score.

STRUCTURE CROSS-CHECK
AF2 reference vs independent ESMFold model: TM=0.939, RMSD 0.45 A over 66 residues (call_id:57c3b919483c40f69624930874de4d58); ESMFold mean CA pLDDT 0.885. Two independent structure channels agree, so ESM-IF1 is operating on a trustworthy backbone.

TOOL FAILURE (reported, not worked around)
dssp failed on BOTH the reference PDB (call_id:4347b81933ec4605a6241b7799e4201a) and the ESMFold artifact (call_id:bc7a93271b4d43dca9d676f25876b755): "did not start with a valid PDB HEADER line". I therefore have NO secondary-structure or solvent-exposure evidence. Burial claims are absent from this analysis by design; any statement about a residue being buried would be unsupported.

KEY METHODOLOGICAL CAUTION - PSSM ARTIFACT
Many pssm_score calls return delta_bits == exactly -1.000 with wt_bits == -0.0704. That is the all-pseudocount signature of a column where NEITHER wt nor mutant is observed (query-only/gapped column). It is ABSENCE of evidence, not negative evidence. Affected here: positions 9, 10, 17, 21, 52, 59, 62. I did not treat these as penalties.
Separately, position 33 has depth=2 and gap_fraction=0.909 (call_id:b81fbda195264714af6b96d8501bc054), so both its PSSM (-1.585) and its conservation (1.0) are statistically empty. D33E rests on the two learned channels only.

STRONGEST RESULT - CONSENSUS REVERSIONS
Columns 49 and 51 are both highly conserved (0.938, entropy 0.267) and the conserved family residue is NOT the E. coli residue: homologs carry ...HLVKVP... where the query carries ...GAVRTR..., i.e. consensus L at 49 and K at 51. Hence A49L and R51K each score +3.459 bits. R51K is corroborated by all three channels (ESM-2 +1.907, ESM-IF +0.51). A49L is the one sharp inter-channel conflict: PSSM +3.459 and ESM-2 +0.529, but ESM-IF -15.1, consistent with a rigid AF2 backbone penalising small->large at a packed site. I kept A49L at rank 5 rather than demoting it, because (a) it carries the strongest evolutionary signal available and (b) it is the single most information-rich experiment in the set - whichever way it reads, one channel is falsified.

RANKING FIELD SEMANTICS
`ranking` scores = raw ESM-2 delta_log_probability for all 100 candidates (the only channel applied uniformly; reproducible, single-source). The top-10 `selected` order deliberately DEVIATES from pure ESM-2 order because it integrates PSSM and ESM-IF. Documented deviations: F17A (ESM-2 +0.079 but ESM-IF -8.65), S18F (ESM-2 +0.024 but PSSM -1.585 and ESM-IF -4.32) and K9E (ESM-IF -8.49) were dropped from the ten despite top-10 ESM-2 ranks; A25Q, A10T, T52L were promoted on ESM-IF/multi-channel agreement.

NOT DONE / LIMITS
No ddG, no MD, no binding calculation, no measured fitness of any kind. openmm_snapshot_potential_delta was deliberately not used: it compares unminimised snapshots and is not a ddG or a variant ranker, and I had no mutant coordinates to feed it. pubmed_search not used; prior literature would not constitute this assay's label. All scores below are model predictions.
